topicRulePayload.sql: SELECT *, topic() AS source_topic, timestamp() AS ingest_ts FROM 'smart-factory/factory/vision/inspection_result'
topicRulePayload.description: Routes vision inspection results forwarded from the local MQTT bridge (mqtt_publisher.py) into IoT Core-connected storage and downstream Lambda processing for predictive maintenance scoring.

additionalRules.description: Routes OEE and PLC status telemetry for cloud-side dashboards and long-term archival.

additionalRules.sql: SELECT * FROM 'smart-factory/factory/plc/conveyor_status' WHERE vibration_rms > 3.5 OR cycle_time_drift_pct > 10
additionalRules.description: Filters telemetry crossing predictive-maintenance thresholds and triggers a maintenance alert Lambda that writes to the maintenance_alerts table in PostgreSQL and publishes to Predictive_Maintenance_Alert.

setup_notes: Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with your AWS account ID before applying with `aws iot create-topic-rule`.

Create the referenced IAM roles (SmartFactoryIoTRepublishRole, SmartFactoryIoTS3Role, SmartFactoryIoTErrorLogRole) with least-privilege policies scoped to the specific S3 bucket, Lambda function, and CloudWatch log group.
The 'smart-factory/' topic prefix matches AWSIoTForwarder.forward() in iot-bridge/mqtt_publisher.py, which republishes local MQTT topics under this prefix.
smart-factory-influx-forwarder and smart-factory-pdm-alert-handler are placeholder Lambda function names; implement them separately or route directly to Kinesis/Timestream if preferred over Lambda.
AWS IoT Core free tier covers a limited number of messages/month, sufficient for a portfolio demo but not sustained production load.
